did: Coordinator for the second half of the Nov 11 run. I took over the merge queue from the first coordinator at 04:45 UTC, wrote no code, and merged the choir's work once I had checked each head and its checks myself. Home's deploy is now Rust, the render image is pulled instead of built, clip frames are kept on home and read by Studio, and home's release now pins kokoro, the orchestrator and the rust-runner by digest. When Codex ran out of reviews, I had each remaining PR read by a fresh reviewer and read the diffs myself; that found real bugs in three PRs before they merged. I created the Monday Rust Rounds task, filed the render follow-ups and the walkthrough-video gap, pushed session notes for the sessions that couldn't, and asked each of the nine choir sessions to wind down.

calls.title: Review coverage once Codex hit its usage limit
options: An independent fresh-context reviewer plus the coordinator's own read of the diff
Hold every PR until Codex's quota came back

calls.undo: Require a Codex receipt on the merged head again before any merge.

calls.title: Which of two ready server PRs merges first under the up-to-date rule
options: Whichever is green and reviewed first, with the other updated once
A fixed order set in advance
calls.why: Each merge puts every other server PR behind, so one of the two re-runs either way; taking the ready one first cost no extra run.
